Not uncommon at all. They're very closely linked. The thing to remember is that even the most disgusting person you know doesn't get sick and doesn't make the people around them sick. Humans are pretty tough creatures, we wouldn't have gotten howevermanyyears without soap otherwise!

The person I'm dating eats food off public tables... so yeah I think I've gotten over that aspect. A big hurdle I have to leap is interrupting my cycle of thoughts because I think about the same thing over and over and over.

Also very common! One helpful thing can be to put the thought aside to be worried about later. OCD can be satisfied by setting aside time to deal with the worry later (be it a set time like for 10 minutes at 10pm or just 'later'). And often, by the time you get to later the problem doesn't seem as big as it was!

Yeah, the thing with OCD + Anxiety is it's an overreaction by your brain trying to alert you to something that you believe is "danger". So, obsessing over things (which is very easily done with OCD!) reinforces to your brain that yes this IS something you need to be alerted to, which leads to it spiralling into a cycle because you're constantly reinforcing the perceived "need" to worry. By putting it off until later the message you're sending your brain is "This isn't really an urgent problem", so the next time the worry occurs it'll carry less weight, and you end up in a positive cycle of reducing the impact it has on your life each time! :)

Exercise

There are effectively two types of exercise: aerobic and anaerobic. Aerobic burns calories and anaerobic works muscle. YOU CAN NOT EXERCISE AWAY A BAD DIET...unless you're the same level athlete as Michael Phelps...which if you're getting anything out of this article you are not. However, it helps. It gives you a bit of leeway to have that special chocolate chip cookie that Barbara down the hall made. Just calculate it into your diet plan. You can fudge a bit if you're doing aerobic exercise because you're burning more calories. Not too many more, but some. On the flip side of this, anaerobic exercise, burns very few calories but will help you build muscle, which tightens everything up and makes you look better. Some people think anaerobic exercise is not worth it, but I wholeheartedly disagree. You will tone up and look thinner/healthier if you build muscle. It sort of pulls everything in place. So this is what it looks like with zero weight loss:
Female lifting

  1. Aerobic exercise , called cardio from here on out, can be anything from running a marathon or walking around the block. It's getting up and moving with limited muscular usage. You just continue to move. There are two basic types of aerobic exercise: HIIT and LISS. LISS, or Low Intensity Steady State, are things like walking, jogging, etc. for a longer period of time at a slower pace. HIIT is High Intensity Interval Training, such as lighter weight crossfit or anything done by Shaun T (The Insanity guy), etc. will effectively kick your butt in a much faster, more intense period of time. The jury is still out as to which one is better overall for calorie burn. However, HIIT usually ends up having some element of anaerobic exercise element as an added benefit. My preference is to do a combination of both as long as you enjoy it. Do what works for you in this arena. I'm not going to break this down. It's pretty simple stuff. You generally just keep going. Hop on a hamster wheel and go.

  2. Anaerobic exercise, called muscle building from here on out, is anything that works your muscles in a strenuous way that causes them to tear and repair themselves. Now this tearing isn't big gash tearing, but micro-tears that cause your body to heal the tears and increase the size of the muscle to accommodate heavier exercise. Without tearing there is no muscle growth. That's how it works in essence. A good rule of thumb is if you do repetitions past 12 and you're still going strong you're doing a more aerobic exercise. Less than six and in most instances you're looking at pure strength training. Between 6 and 12 is generally your sweet spot for what's known as hypertrophy, or maximum muscle building. Yes ladies. You're looking for hypertrophy as well.

  3. Know how to lift...bro (or brosefina)? Here's a handy dandy chart of the full body experience you should be focusing on working. The exercises listed are optimal or near optimal exercises for the body parts identified. These are the muscle groups you should be focusing on. I don't know about you but ain't nobody got time for that. We can't all do all the exercises all the time. We would have no time for anything else. Fortunately, we have compound exercises, such as the weighted squat, the deadlift, the bench press and the overhead press.

  4. Compound lifts will target multiple areas at the same time, maximizing your gym time, kicking your butt, and giving you cool "bro numbers" you can spout off the next time someone asks "Bro, what do you bench/squat/pull?" So that's the standard three everyone mentions; Flat bench press, weighted squat and deadlift. Everybody wants these done with a barbell, but they can all be done alternately with different equipment in varying situations. There are a whole host of alternate exercises with different weights, such as dumbbells, kettlebells or even bands, that can be substituted. Just remember to work within your own personal skill and ability. WARNING: THESE THREE EXERCISES CAN PERMANENTLY INJURE YOU IF DONE WRONG! Seriously though, you need to know how to do these exercises properly or your form will be off and you'll injure yourself. There is no need to rush under a barbell if you don't know what you're doing. But if you familiarize yourself with these three exercises you can minimize your gym time and maximize your muscle gain.

  5. Other major exercises are still highly important and frequently overlooked. Exercising all of your body parts in multiple ways is crucial to all around muscular growth, development and fitness. Here's a nice article on Bodybuilding that covers the big three, but also goes into full explanation of several other helpful exercises. Please go through it all to understand how to do them. I would suggest doing pretty much all of them or some variation at least once a week.

  6. Progressive overload is how you're going to get through this without killing yourself the first day and quitting. If you're just starting, start small. Only do maybe 3-4 muscle exercises to start getting yourself familiar with equipment and your capacity. You should start with exercises working your back/abs, your legs, your chest and your shoulders. This will be your main focus for life. Every week increase the weight by 5-10 pounds in sets of 8-12 for most exercises. If you feel you can do more, do more. If you want to incorporate a new exercise, try it at the end of your routine or work it in. Record what you do each week. You will improve every single time you hit the gym for a really long time. Your "newbie gains" will excite you and get you encouraged to hit the gym. What new lift will you try? Will you be able to do a full 12 reps and move up to the next weight? Progressive overload is continually overloading your muscles in a program that increases weight over a gradual period of time. Once you are in a full workout routine you should expect to spend maybe an hour to an hour and a half in the gym. This can last until about the time you see your abs as long as your eating right. Your gains will eventually slow, you will plateau, you will try new things. Please remember to keep doing your primary exercises as those are the ones that got you to where you are and will keep you there.

Final word here is that THIS DOES NOT HAPPEN OVERNIGHT. This happens over an extended period of slow progress. Perseverance and adherence are what you get you to where you want to be. There are no shortcuts. No magic beans. No special bracelets. Expect it to take longer than expected or planned, but continue on with it and see it through. Diet and exercise. Move less and eat more...explained.

So, there you go. That's how to do it in a nutshell. That's how pretty much everyone who succeeds does it, with some variance of course. Have you gone through a similar process and ended up with awesome abs? Still just taking six pictures every month? I didn't think so. You're snapping pics of your new muscles and sending them to anybody who hasn't blocked you on facebook. Admit it.
